gaps.sentence: He would be healthier if he ___ so much red meat.
gaps.hint: an unreal present habit, past simple
gaps.explanation: For an unreal present habit, the if-clause uses the past simple: did not eat.

gaps.sentence: I wish you ___ your shoes in the middle of the floor!
gaps.hint: irritation about a habit, wish would
gaps.explanation: 'Wish' plus 'would' expresses irritation about a habit you want changed: would not leave.

gaps.sentence: If I ___ a million euros, I would travel the world for a year.
gaps.explanation: Second conditionals use the past simple after 'if' for unreal presents: won.

gaps.sentence: If the taxi ___ in five minutes, we are going to miss our flight.
gaps.hint: real future risk in the if-clause
gaps.explanation: Real future conditions take the present simple in the if-clause: does not arrive.

gaps.sentence: I will note the reference number in case I ___ it later.
gaps.hint: in case means as a precaution
gaps.explanation: 'In case' describes a precaution and takes the present simple: need.

gaps.sentence: She wishes she ___ the job offer when it came.
gaps.explanation: Regret about a past decision takes the past perfect: had accepted.

gaps.sentence: Unless the road ___, the coach cannot use this route.
gaps.explanation: 'Unless' takes the present simple, here in the passive: is widened.

gaps.sentence: If it ___ tomorrow, the match will be cancelled.
gaps.explanation: In first conditionals the if-clause takes the present simple even with future meaning: rains.
